name: cna-web
description: Analyst workstation for the Criminal Network Analysis system (zone Z0).
//dependencies: Two runtime dependencies. This is a deliberate ceiling, not an accident of a
small app.
No graph library. d3-force, cytoscape, sigma and vis-network were all
considered and all rejected for the same reason: each wants to own both the
layout and the drawing, and the drawing is where this system's honesty
controls live. Edge opacity carries source reliability, dash pattern carries
the intelligence assessment, community boundaries are open arcs rather than
closed hulls, and the analyst's identity is painted into the pixels. Bending a
general-purpose renderer into those constraints is more code than
src/graph/render.ts, and it leaves the constraints as configuration that a
later contributor can switch off. Layout is ~90 lines of Barnes-Hut-free
force integration in src/graph/layout.ts, which is enough for the 500-element
ceiling the API enforces.
No CSS-in-JS. styled-components and emotion inject <style> elements at
runtime, which requires style-src 'unsafe-inline'. Weakening the CSP so the
styling is more ergonomic is the wrong trade in a system holding intelligence
data. Plain CSS with custom properties, and React's style prop where a value
is genuinely dynamic (that writes through CSSOM, which CSP does not gate).
No state manager, no data-fetching library. Every response carries a
disclosure envelope and an audit sequence number that must be shown to the
analyst; a cache that replays a response would show a disclosure notice for a
disclosure that was never audited. See src/api/client.ts.
No router. Deep-linkable URLs would put entity ids and case numbers in browser
history and in the referrer of anything the analyst opens next.
